docs.title: Your own backend
docs.text: Every family has a base class: offsite_backup.stores.base.Store, offsite_backup.encryption.base.Sealer, offsite_backup.databases.base.DatabaseSource, offsite_backup.media.base.MediaSource, offsite_backup.config.base.ConfigSource, offsite_backup.notifiers.base.Notifier. Name your subclass by its dotted path in BACKEND; the package needs no change. Declare REQUIRED, SIGNALS and BINARIES on the class to take part in E001, the on/off decision and E003, and override check() (offline) and deploy_check() (network, run by check --deploy) for anything else. A path that is not a subclass of the family's base is E002.

docs.title: Stores: S3
docs.text:
'STORE': {
    'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store',
    'ENDPOINT_URL': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT', ''),
    'REGION': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_REGION', ''),
    'BUCKET': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_BUCKET', ''),
    'ACCESS_KEY': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY', ''),
    'SECRET_KEY': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY', ''),
    'LOCK_DAYS': 13,
},

pip install 'django-offsite-backup[s3]'. Any S3-compatible server; what each provider needs is on S3 providers. Options are in Settings.

docs.title: What the bucket must be
docs.text:
why checked by versioning enabled Object Lock needs it; it comes with Object Lock E005 Object Lock enabled the immutability itself — and it can only be switched on when the bucket is created E005 a default retention rule: COMPLIANCE, LOCK_DAYS days multipart uploads take their lock date from it (below) E006 KEEP_NIGHTS greater than LOCK_DAYS so rotation only ever meets objects whose lock has run out E007

E005 and E006 read the bucket, so they run under python manage.py check --deploy only; a plain manage.py never reaches S3.

docs.title: How an object is written
docs.text:
Every upload passes the lock as arguments — ObjectLockMode=COMPLIANCE and ObjectLockRetainUntilDate=now + LOCK_DAYS — and then reads it back with HeadObject. The object must have landed COMPLIANCE and locked until at least the date asked, less one hour of slack for clock skew. If it did not, the pass fails with BackupUnlockedError before rotation runs, so an unprotected backup is never what pushes a protected one out.

Each rule answers something measured on a real S3 provider:

  • A single PUT ignored the bucket's default retention. The bucket's default read back as COMPLIANCE, and new objects still landed GOVERNANCE. So the mode and the date are arguments of every upload, never left to the bucket.
  • GOVERNANCE protects nothing against the key that writes: that key can delete through it with "bypass governance retention", and some providers have no IAM to withhold the permission. Only COMPLIANCE. LOCK_DAYS sets the days; the mode is not configurable.
  • A multipart upload kept the mode but took its date from the bucket's default rule, not from the request. Without a default rule of exactly LOCK_DAYS days, every object above one part — every media volume — fails the read-back. That is E006.
  • One PUT stops at 5 GB (EntityTooLarge). Uploads go multipart in 64 MiB parts above 64 MiB, and media is cut into volumes of at most 4 GiB.
  • On a versioned bucket, a delete without a version id only writes a delete marker — every byte stays stored and billed. Rotation lists and deletes versions, markers included.

The client retries each request up to five times (botocore's standard mode), and every listing follows pagination to its end.

docs.title: Credentials: only the ones you name
docs.text:
The client is built from ENDPOINT_URL, REGION, ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY and nothing else. botocore's default credential chain is not consulted: a stray ~/.aws, an instance role or an AWS_* variable would otherwise send backups somewhere nobody chose, reporting success.

Give the backup its own key, allowed to reach this bucket (and, where the provider can narrow it, this prefix) and nothing else. What it needs is in S3 providers.

docs.title: Keys and prefixes
docs.text:
<PREFIX>/<kind>/<stamp>[.without-media][.<NNN>].<suffix>

acme/prod/db/2026-03-10T03-00Z.sql.zst.age
acme/prod/db-analytics/2026-03-10T03-00Z.sql.zst.age
acme/prod/media/2026-03-10T03-00Z.001.tar.age
acme/prod/media/2026-03-10T03-00Z.002.tar.age
acme/prod/config/2026-03-10T03-00Z.tar.zst.age
acme/prod/db/2026-03-10T14-12Z.without-media.sql.zst.age
acme/prod/config/2026-03-10T14-12Z.without-media.tar.zst.age

Several projects can share one bucket, a prefix each; rotation is strictly scoped to <PREFIX>/<kind>/ with the trailing slash, so acme/prod/ never touches acme/prod-old/. Whether they should share depends on what a key can reach — on some providers a key reaches every bucket of its project, and then one leaked key exposes every project in it. S3 providers says which.

docs.title: Without a lock
docs.text: LOCK_DAYS: 0 uploads without lock arguments and reads nothing back; check --deploy then only checks the bucket is reachable. Use it for a bucket that cannot have Object Lock — knowing that the key on the server can then delete every backup (Security model).

docs.title: Stores: directory
docs.text:
'STORE': {
    'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.filesystem.DirectoryStore',
    'ROOT': '/backups',
},

A directory on disk, or a Docker volume mounted into the container that runs the backup. No extra, no driver.

The same object names as on S3 (<ROOT>/<PREFIX>/<kind>/<stamp>...), the same encryption, the same whole-night rotation, the same morning check.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
No immutability. Whoever can write to the directory can delete from it — the application, anyone who gets a shell in its container, and a mistaken rm -r. Kept on the machine it protects, it answers "somebody dropped a table", not "the machine is gone" and not "somebody got in". manage.py check says so on every start:

?: (offsite_backup.W001) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE'] is a directory: backups there can be deleted by whoever can write to it.
    HINT: Fine for a fast local copy; keep the disaster copy in an S3 store with Object Lock.

That is a warning, not an error, on purpose: a directory store is a legitimate choice for a staging machine, or for a disk that is in fact mounted from elsewhere. Silence it with SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ['offsite_backup.W001'] once you have decided.

In 0.1.0 a project has one store. Several at once — a local volume for a fast restore and S3 for disaster, each with its own retention — is on the roadmap.

docs.title: How files are written
docs.text:
• Each object is copied to <name>.part, flushed to disk, set to mode 0600, and renamed into place, so a reader never sees half a file; a .part left by a crash is ignored by listings and rotation.
  • Every directory the store creates, ROOT included, gets mode 0700; directories that already exist keep theirs.
  • A key that would resolve outside ROOT is refused.
  • A directory keeps no history: one "version" per file, and a delete removes it.

docs.title: Docker volume
docs.text:
services:
  web:
    volumes:
      - backups:/backups
  worker:
    volumes:
      - backups:/backups
volumes:
  backups: {}

Mount it into every service that runs a pass — the worker that runs the nightly task and the service the deploy pass runs in — or each writes its own, unseen half.

docs.title: System checks
docs.text:
The package registers two checks with Django's checks framework, both tagged offsite_backup:

check runs on reaches the network codes settings every manage.py command that runs checks, and manage.py check no E001–E003, E007, E008, W001–W005 deploy manage.py check --deploy only yes — the bucket and each database E004–E006

Nothing is checked on a machine where backups are off (Settings). The deploy check is also skipped while any E001 is outstanding — fix the settings first.

python manage.py check                          # offline
python manage.py check --deploy                 # adds the bucket's lock and pg_dump's version
python manage.py check --tag offsite_backup     # this package's checks only
python manage.py check --deploy --fail-level WARNING

Codes are stable: a code never changes meaning. Each is explained, with its fix, on Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: code when where it comes from offsite_backup.E001 backups are configured by halves: PREFIX, a STORE/ENCRYPTION BACKEND, every source, or a backend's required option is empty; KEEP_NIGHTS is not a positive integer. Also: FORMAT not plain/custom, VOLUME_BYTES out of range, a Telegram TOPIC_ID that is not an integer, a GUARD['CACHE'] missing from CACHES settings offsite_backup.E002 a BACKEND path that is empty, does not import, is not the family's base class — or names a shipped backend whose driver extra is not installed settings offsite_backup.E003 a binary a backend runs is not on PATH: age, pg_dump, pg_restore, psql, or the program COMPRESS / DECOMPRESS names settings offsite_backup.E004 pg_dump is older than a database server it must dump deploy offsite_backup.E005 the bucket cannot be read, is not versioned, has no Object Lock, or its lock configuration cannot be read deploy offsite_backup.E006 the bucket's default retention is missing, not COMPLIANCE, or not LOCK_DAYS days deploy offsite_backup.E007 KEEP_NIGHTS is not greater than LOCK_DAYS settings offsite_backup.E008 RECIPIENTS holds a private age key, or something that is not an age recipient settings

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text: code when offsite_backup.W001 the store is a DirectoryStore — no immutability, on the machine it protects offsite_backup.W002 encryption is the test Passthrough — nothing is encrypted offsite_backup.W003 the once-per-night guard uses a LocMemCache or DummyCache offsite_backup.W004 a test run with NOTIFY set and notifiers not silenced offsite_backup.W005 a media ROOT, a CONFIG path or the RENDER_ENV file does not exist here

docs.title: Silencing
docs.text:
A warning you have decided to live with goes in SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS:

SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ['offsite_backup.W001']  # a directory store on staging, on purpose

Do not silence an error to get a deploy through: every one of them is a backup that would fail, or one that would succeed while protecting nothing.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text: Run manage.py check --deploy with the production settings in the image you are about to deploy — it is where E003 (a binary missing from a slimmed image) and E004 (a pg_dump older than the server after a database upgrade) are cheapest to find. Mind what it cannot see: without the store credentials the machine counts as off and nothing at all is checked, and a database it cannot connect to is skipped by E004 rather than reported.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Two things a project's tests need from this package: that they never post to a real chat, and a way to test their own backup wiring without S3, age or a network.

docs.title: Tests never notify
docs.text:
A CI job that inherited the production bot token from the project's variables once posted the test suite's backup messages to the team's chat. So:

  • pytest: installing the package registers a pytest plugin (pytest11 entry point) that silences every notifier able to reach the network, from the first test to the last. Nothing to configure.

  • Django's test runner: use the shipped runner, or mix it into yours:

    TEST_RUNNER = 'offsite_backup.testing.OffsiteBackupTestRunner'

    from offsite_backup.testing import OffsiteBackupTestRunner


class ProjectRunner(OffsiteBackupTestRunner, YourRunner): ...

"Silenced" means: a notifier whose class says REACHES_NETWORK = True — Telegram, django-aiogram, and any third-party notifier unless it says otherwise — is not called. LogNotifier still logs, and capture() still sees every message. Under a test run that is not silenced and has NOTIFY set, manage.py check warns W004.

And still: keep production notifier tokens out of the CI test job. The silence covers this package; it does not cover your own code, other packages, or a script that runs manage.py outside the test runner. In GitHub Actions, give the token only to the deploy job's environment; in GitLab CI, make the variable protected and scope it to the production environment, so the test job never sees it.

To silence a block by hand (a script, a REPL):

from offsite_backup.testing import silence

with silence():
    ...

docs.title: Asserting on messages: capture()
docs.text:
from offsite_backup.testing import capture


def test_deploy_pass_says_media_is_left(configured):
    with capture() as said:
        call_command('backup_offsite', '--without-media', '--reason', 'deploy')
    outcome, text = said[-1]
    assert outcome.kind == 'written'
    assert 'Media: left to the nightly pass' in text

capture() collects every (outcome, text) formatted inside the block, whatever NOTIFY holds — silenced or not, with or without notifiers.

docs.title: A fake S3: FakeS3 and use_fake_s3
docs.text:
from offsite_backup.testing import FakeS3, use_fake_s3


@pytest.fixture
def fake_s3():
    fake = FakeS3(page_size=2, multipart_threshold=1024)
    fake.bucket('backups')  # Object Lock on, default COMPLIANCE 13 days
    with use_fake_s3(fake):
        yield fake

Inside use_fake_s3() every S3 client the package builds — the store's and S3Source's — is the fake. It is in memory and behaves like the providers backups are kept at, including where they bite:

  • versions and delete markers; a delete without a version id adds a marker;
  • Object Lock: a locked version refuses deletion (AccessDenied);
  • pagination, page_size items per page, so loops over pages are exercised;
  • a single PUT without lock arguments lands GOVERNANCE, whatever the bucket's default;
  • a multipart upload (from multipart_threshold bytes) keeps the mode but takes its date from the bucket's default rule — none without one;
  • a single PUT above put_limit is refused with EntityTooLarge.

fake.bucket(name, versioned=..., lock_enabled=..., default_mode=..., default_days=...) creates or reconfigures a bucket; fake.buckets[name].keys holds every version; fake.calls records uploads and deletes; FakeS3(clock=...) moves time for lock expiry. put_object() seeds a media bucket for S3Source.

docs.title: No age on the CI machine: Passthrough
docs.text:
'ENCRYPTION': {'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.testing.Passthrough', 'RECIPIENTS': ['age1test']},
'COMPRESS': [],

cat instead of age, both ways. It raises W002 on every check — nothing it writes is encrypted — so it cannot reach production unnoticed. An empty COMPRESS drops the zstd stage as well.

docs.title: Media on disk: media_tree
docs.text:
from offsite_backup.testing import media_tree

root = media_tree(tmp_path / 'media', {'a.jpg': b'a' * 300, 'sub/b.png': b'b' * 300})

Writes {relative path: bytes} under a root and returns it — a DirectorySource ROOT.

docs.title: A whole wiring test
docs.text:
import pytest
from django.core.management import call_command

from offsite_backup.testing import FakeS3, capture, media_tree, use_fake_s3


@pytest.fixture
def configured(settings, tmp_path):
    fake = FakeS3()
    fake.bucket('backups')
    settings.OFFSITE_BACKUP = {
        'PREFIX': 'acme/test',
        'STORE': {
            'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store',
            'BUCKET': 'backups',
            'ACCESS_KEY': 'k',
            'SECRET_KEY': 's',
        },
        'ENCRYPTION': {'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.testing.Passthrough', 'RECIPIENTS': ['age1test']},
        'COMPRESS': [],
        'MEDIA': [
            {
                'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.media.filesystem.DirectorySource',
                'ROOT': str(media_tree(tmp_path / 'media', {'a.jpg': b'a'})),
            },
        ],
    }
    with use_fake_s3(fake):
        yield fake


def test_nightly_pass_writes_a_volume(configured):
    with capture() as said:
        call_command('backup_offsite', '--reason', 'nightly')
    keys = list(configured.buckets['backups'].keys)
    assert any(key.startswith('acme/test/media/') and key.endswith('.001.tar.age') for key in keys)
    assert said[-1][0].kind == 'written'

A database source needs pg_dump and a real PostgreSQL; test that in an integration job, or stand a DatabaseSource subclass of your own in for it.

docs.title: The guard in tests
docs.text: run_nightly() claims the night in the GUARD['CACHE']. Tests that call it twice in one "night" see the second skipped — clear the cache between tests, or pass 'GUARD': {'ENABLED': False}.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Every system check code first, then what goes wrong at run time, then the S3 behaviours this package was built around.

docs.title: E001 — configured by halves
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E001) Backups are configured by halves; these are unset: OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']['SECRET_KEY'], OFFSITE_BACKUP['ENCRYPTION']['BACKEND']
    HINT: Set every one, or leave the store credentials empty to turn backups off on this machine.

Cause. Something switched backups on — a store credential or a ROOT (the rule) — and something they need is empty. Usually one environment variable missing from one container.

Fix. Set every setting the message names. If this machine should not back up at all (a laptop, a CI job), make all the store options empty, or set 'ENABLED': False.

The same code is used for values that are present but wrong, each with its own message:

message fix ... (a positive integer, got ...) for KEEP_NIGHTS an int ≥ 1 ['FORMAT'] is ...; expected one of plain, custom 'plain' or 'custom' ['VOLUME_BYTES'] is ...; expected more than 20480 bytes and at most 5 GB the default 4 GiB is right for almost everyone ['TOPIC_ID'] is ..., not an integer the numeric topic id, or empty GUARD['CACHE'] is ..., which CACHES does not define name a cache alias that exists ... (nothing to back up) set at least one of DATABASES, MEDIA, CONFIG

docs.title: E002 — a backend that cannot be loaded
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E002) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']['BACKEND'] is S3Store, but its driver is not installed.
    HINT: pip install "django-offsite-backup[s3]"

Cause. The extra is not installed in this image, the dotted path has a typo, or it names a class that is not a subclass of the family's base (a Store where a Sealer is expected, for example).

Fix. Install the extra the hint names; otherwise copy the path from Settings — offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store, not offsite_backup.stores.S3Store.

docs.title: E003 — a binary is missing
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E003) OFFSITE_BACKUP['DATABASES'] runs `pg_dump`, which is not on PATH.
    HINT: Install pg_dump in the image that runs the backup.

Cause. The image that runs the pass lacks pg_dump, age or zstd. Slim base images do.

Fix. Install it in that image — the worker's, and the one the deploy pass runs in (Installation).

docs.title: E004 — pg_dump older than the server
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E004) pg_dump is 16, older than the server of 'default' (18).
    HINT: Install the PostgreSQL 18 client (e.g. postgresql-client-18) in the image.

Cause. The database was upgraded and the application image was not. pg_dump refuses to dump a newer server; every pass would fail.

Fix. Install the client of the server's major (or newer) from the PostgreSQL apt repository. Deploy checks only (check --deploy).

docs.title: E005 — the bucket cannot hold a locked backup
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E005) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']: bucket 'acme-backups' has no Object Lock.
    HINT: Object Lock can only be enabled when a bucket is created: create a new bucket with it, or set LOCK_DAYS to 0 to store without immutability.

Four messages share the code:

message cause fix bucket ... could not be read (<code>) wrong ENDPOINT_URL, bucket name, key, or a network block check each; the S3 error code is in the brackets bucket ... is not versioned created without Object Lock a new bucket, created with Object Lock the Object Lock configuration of ... could not be read the key may not read it (GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration) grant it (S3 providers) bucket ... has no Object Lock created without it a new bucket, created with Object Lock; it cannot be switched on later on most providers. Move PREFIX there and let the old bucket's objects expire

docs.title: E006 — no default rule, or the wrong one
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E006) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']: bucket 'acme-backups' has default retention none, not COMPLIANCE 13 days.
    HINT: Multipart uploads (anything over 64 MiB) take their lock date from this rule, not from the request; set a default rule of COMPLIANCE, 13 days.

Cause. The bucket has Object Lock but no default retention rule, a GOVERNANCE one, or one of a different number of days than LOCK_DAYS. Every object uploaded in parts — every media volume, any large database — would land with the bucket's date (or none) and fail the read-back.

Fix. put-object-lock-configuration with COMPLIANCE and Days equal to LOCK_DAYS (S3 providers).

docs.title: E007 — retention not longer than the lock
docs.text:
Cause. KEEP_NIGHTS <= LOCK_DAYS. Rotation would meet locked objects every night and leave them, and the folder would hold more than you think.

Fix. Keep at least one night more than the lock: 14 nights, 13 days.

docs.title: E008 — not a public key in RECIPIENTS
docs.text:
Cause. RECIPIENTS holds an AGE-SECRET-KEY-… (the private half), or a string that is none of age1…, ssh-ed25519 …, ssh-rsa … — often several keys in one comma-separated string, or a quoted value with the quotes kept.

Fix. The public half only (age-keygen -y key.txt prints it); a list for several. If a private key was there, it has been on the server: make a new pair, and treat every backup sealed to the old one as readable by whoever had the server.

docs.title: W001 — a directory store
docs.text: No immutability, on the machine it protects. Fine for a fast local copy or a staging machine; silence it there (SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS). For production, the disaster copy belongs in S3 with Object Lock.

docs.title: W002 — Passthrough encryption
docs.text: The test sealer is configured: nothing is encrypted. It belongs in test settings only. Use offsite_backup.encryption.age_cli.AgeCli.

docs.title: W003 — the guard's cache is not shared
docs.text: GUARD['CACHE'] is a LocMemCache or DummyCache. Each worker has its own, so two schedulers can both run tonight. Point it at Redis, Memcached or the database cache, or turn the guard off if exactly one scheduler can ever run ('GUARD': {'ENABLED': False}).

docs.title: W004 — notifiers in a test run
docs.text: A test run (pytest, or manage.py test) with NOTIFY set and not silenced — with pytest the plugin silences it, so this means Django's runner without OffsiteBackupTestRunner. Set TEST_RUNNER (Testing), and keep production notifier tokens out of the CI test job.

docs.title: W005 — a path is missing here
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.W005) OFFSITE_BACKUP['CONFIG']: /app/deploy not found here.
    HINT: Mount the deployment directory (read-only) into every container that runs the backup.

A media ROOT, a CONFIG path or the RENDER_ENV file is not there in this container. Usually a volume mounted into the web service and not the worker, or the other way round.

docs.title: backup_offsite: not configured on this machine, nothing to do — on production
docs.text: None of the switching options reached this process: the variables are in one service's env_file and not the one that ran the command, or a .env was not loaded. manage.py shell -c "from offsite_backup import conf; print(conf.read().values['STORE'])" shows what the process sees.

docs.title: BackupUnlockedError: ... landed GOVERNANCE until ... / landed unlocked
docs.text: The object did not land with the lock asked. A short date on a large object means the bucket's default rule is missing or different (E006); unlocked means the bucket has no Object Lock (E005). The pass stops before rotation, so nothing older was deleted. Fix the bucket and run check --deploy.

docs.title: PipelineError from pg_dump
docs.text: The tail of pg_dump's stderr follows. Common ones: server version mismatch (E004), password authentication failed (the alias's PASSWORD), permission denied for table (the role cannot read every table — dump with the owner role, or grant SELECT). The other databases, the media and the configuration still went up.

docs.title: PipelineError from age
docs.text: Usually a malformed recipient that slipped past E008 (several keys in one string), or — in a restore — the wrong identity: no identity matched any of the recipients.

docs.title: A database restore says "is not empty"
docs.text: backup_restore --apply refuses a database that has tables. Restore into an empty one, or add --clean to drop and recreate the public schema first.

docs.title: The morning check reports a database missing that was just added
docs.text: With ALIASES computed at run time, a new database has no backup until its first night. Run a whole pass (backup_offsite), or back_up_database('<alias>') from a shell. Not --only db in a project with media: that pass is marked .without-media. and does not count.

docs.title: Telegram: no message, Telegram refused the backup message
docs.text: The description in the log says why: message thread not found is a wrong TOPIC_ID; chat not found a wrong CHAT_ID or a bot that is not a member; can't parse entities would mean a custom formatter that did not escape its values.

docs.title: The nightly task ran twice
docs.text: The guard's cache is not shared (W003), or GUARD['ENABLED'] is off. With a shared cache the second run logs Nightly backup skipped: tonight is being written.

docs.title: The deploy waits a long time for the backup
docs.text: The deploy pass includes media: add --without-media. If the database itself is the long part, a lighter COMPRESS (['zstd', '-10', '-T0', '-q']) trades size for time.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: 0.1.0 is the first release; there is nothing to upgrade from yet.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The package follows semantic versioning, with one rule spelled out because it is the one that bites in a backup tool:

  • A settings rename, a removed setting, or a default that flips is a major version. A default decides what a machine backs up and how long it keeps it; changing it under a minor bump would change production in silence.
  • Object names are a compatibility surface. A release that changes how keys are named keeps reading the old names — for rotation, the morning check and restore — until objects under them have rotated out, and says so here.
  • Check codes are stable. A code never changes meaning; a new check gets a new code.
  • Anything else that changes behaviour is a minor version, and is in the Changelog.

While the major version is 0, a minor release may still carry a breaking change, and if it does this page says exactly what to change.

docs.title: How to upgrade
docs.text:
1. Read the Changelog between your version and the new one, and this page.
  2. Bump the pin; run python manage.py check --deploy in the new image.
  3. Run backup_offsite --reason manual once after deploying and read the message.
  4. Run the restore drill if the release touched naming, encryption or restore.
